AFWD.justification: The algebraic operation mapping pairs of elements to their sum in the real vector space

AREV.justification: The operation of removing elements to isolate the intersection

CLINK.justification: The sequential ordering of construction steps across all ordinals up to the continuum

ENGAGR.justification: The dual nature of a Hamel basis as both linearly independent and spanning the entire space

EVALF.justification: The selection of a point into the complement to ensure S meets every Borel set

EVALT.justification: The successful selection of a point into the Bernstein set

FFUSE.justification: The union of the constructed Bernstein set and its complement back into the continuum

FSPLIT.justification: The bifurcation of the continuum into a sequence of disjoint Borel subsets for selection

IFIX.justification: The irreversible selection of representatives from non-empty sets that cannot be undone

IMSCRIB.justification: The underlying set which remains itself throughout the partitioning process

TANCH.justification: The final verification that the intersection is empty within the real line topology

VINIT.justification: The state prior to the construction of specific sets or the invocation of the Axiom of Choice

phase_3.false_description: The condition where a point belongs to the complement of S
phase_3.true_description: The condition where a point belongs to the Bernstein set S

steps.domain_action: Assume the existence of the real line R as a vector space over the rationals Q
Invoke the Axiom of Choice to well-order the collection of all uncountable closed subsets of R
Enumerate all Borel sets B_alpha for alpha < 2^aleph_0
Begin transfinite induction to construct S and its complement
Select x_alpha into S from B_alpha not previously chosen
Select y_alpha into S-complement from B_alpha not previously chosen
Complete the construction of the Bernstein set S
Identify the Hamel basis A for R over Q
Define the sum set A + A as the set of all a1 + a2 for a1, a2 in A
Test the intersection of A + A and S
Consider the linear independence of A against the density of S
Assume an element z exists in both A + A and S
Trace the algebraic dependency of z back to the basis A
Fix the contradiction that S cannot contain any uncountable closed set
Reconcile the algebraic structure with the set-theoretic construction

phase_5.alfs_store: The continuum hypothesis and well-ordering theorem
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Set membership relations and subset inclusions

phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The information gain in the construction is balanced by the exhaustion of the continuum's Borel subsets
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Rigidly defined Bernstein set and Hamel basis
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Undefined subsets of the real line
